title: Mailbox id refusal tests: assert the echoed prefix and cut-off, and the numeric-acknowledge refusal message
outcome: The malformed-id and numeric-acknowledge tests distinguish the behaviour they cover from neighbouring refusals.
acceptance: The over-long malformed-id case uses characters distinguishable across the 96-character cut-off and asserts that the 400 echoes exactly the first 96 input characters, omits the rest, and states the full length.
The numeric-acknowledge test for domain members asserts the central-domain refusal message, not only the 400 status, so it fails if the request is refused as a malformed id instead.
